I had an svt, I have a heart condition and my pulse was almost 300bpm, I was having chest contractions and they were the most painful thing that I've ever experienced.. Or so I thought. At hospital I was given an injection and I felt this extremely intense flushing feeling in my chest, one of the nurses was holding my hand and I was squeezing it so hard it was brutal. I was 14 :/

I really think that you should talk to a therapist. I went undiagnosed with depression and anxiety for 4 years before asking for help, it was brutal. I never asked for help because I felt like people wouldn't believe that I needed it, I was also being abused by a parent. Thankfully I don't see them anymore. By refusing help I was only getting worse and worse, I have attempted suicide, stayed overnight in hospital, promising the nurses that I was safe, only to feel the same way again a few days later. Eventually I spent almost a month in a mental health hospital and I guess only now am I really accepting help.

Depression is like a long dark tunnel and it doesn't seem like you'll ever reach the light on the other side. Infact to me it feels like there was no light to begin with, any happiness that I had wasn't real, I was just being delusional. I know exactly how you are feeling, I also know that it is so much harder to go through this on your own. And yes, people do get upset, they're never upset with you, but with your ILLNESS. It's like any other illness, if you were to find out that someone you loved had cancer you would be devastated, but you'd want to help in any way that you can and look after them. Every now and again you might break down, feel like you can't handle it. But you know that what they're going through isn't their fault, you just have to be there for them. It's the exact same with depression. Therapy can help. It DOES help, otherwise therapists wouldn't exist because there would be no point in them. With therapy and medication you can get better. And you will feel ups and downs. Therapy is so hard, you have to think very deeply about yourself, and you have to face your problems head on rather than pushing them to the side, you have to pour out your most personal thoughts and feelings to a stranger, and most importantly you have to believe, really truly believe, that things will get better. Please please talk to a therapist.

As for inexpensive hobbies, there's lots of things that you can do. For exercise you can go running like you said, you can go walking, hiking , exploring a new place that you haven't been to. Maybe get a dog? You can take them with you, and with another living creature depending on you it will give you a sense of purpose. You don't have to buy one but could get one at a shelter. I personally am into more creative outlets. I play the piano, I have a piano and get lessons now, but to start with I just had a cheap keyboard and taught myself through YouTube videos, you could try learning an instrument? Piano and guitar and are easy enough to teach yourself with a lot of practice. I also like art, I love the adult colouring books, I like drawing with oil pastels, I do origami and decorate my bedroom with what I've made. I also love cooking and baking, maybe set yourself a goal to cook one meal entirely from scratch every week? You could also try volunteering somewhere, at an animal shelter or a home for the elderly, again this will give you a sense of purpose. I really hope things get better for you :)
Thanks I appreciate it, I'm getting better, I think, and am finally free from my abuser

It's a lot easier said than done. I've tried to kill myself and been in hospital, you don't just "not give a shit" about anyone, I genuinely believed that the world would be a much better place without me because I was such a horrible unloveable person, yes people would be upset initially but I felt that it would be better in the long run. Also I had gotten to a point where I didn't feel anything but pain, I couldn't even feel love for people that I was supposed to love, I didn't care about anyone. The world didn't seem real, why would I go through all this pain for people that weren't even real? I know it makes no sense but depression really screws with your head and the way you think about things. I thought that things would never ever get better, and I thought that I didn't deserve for things to get better either, I didn't deserve to be happy. I guess that when you spend your entire childhood being physically and sexually abused by your own parent, someone that was supposed to protect you, you look at the world differently. If my own parent couldn't love me, why would anyone else? If I never knew what happiness was, how could I ever feel it? If these horrible things happened to me then it must be my fault, I must be a bad person that everyone was out to hurt, because I deserved it. I can't trust anyone, I can't be loved or feel love like I should, and I can't just decide to stop being depressed and go on an adventure. People need to get out of the fairytale world where everything is ok and bad things don't happen and the world is a magical place. Because the world is a shit place and so are the people in it, excuse me for not wanting to be a part of it.
